correctness.rationale: For any graph, conditioning on the first uniformly feasible edge gives an exact deletion recurrence. Path and spider edge classifications give the stated difference recurrence, with exact forcing b_L of alternating sign and strictly decreasing magnitude. Pairwise induction proves every d_L>0 for all L>=2, independent of finite tests. The seven-vertex values are exact. Sharpness below seven is an exhaustive Prüfer-word census with an exact Fraction recurrence for every proper KC shift, plus independent full edge-order enumeration of the witnesses. The verifier was executed from its current included source.

originality.rationale: Primary accessible literature distinguishes vertex greedy independent sets, worst-case forest approximation ratios, and random-graph expected behavior from a fixed-tree local KC-shift sign classification. Searches under KC/GTS, random edge greedy matching, dimer adsorption, path/spider aliases, and exact small-n witness returned no equivalent theorem. Full Dyer–Frieze 1991 material is not available and remains a genuine priority risk, not a negative search certificate.
residual_risks: The Dyer–Frieze 1991 fixed-forest analysis was not available in full; the abstract does not exclude an uncited finite example.
Other unindexed dimer adsorption or tree-shift literature might contain equivalent identities; independent historical verification remains outstanding.

value.rationale: KC/GTS tree shifting is a natural structural order used to establish exact tree extremal results. This finding provides both sign directions for a natural stochastic matching invariant, a rigorous infinite family of positive shifts, and an exhaustive sharp first-failure boundary at seven vertices. It is neither a purely finite arbitrary slice nor a restatement of a global approximation bound.
